[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The null_resource updates a Forge role trust policy to name the Lambda execution role as a principal, but it does not wait for the Lambda module to create that role. Ensure the role exists before applying the trust-policy update.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The provisioner updates Forge role trust policies to name the Lambda execution role as a principal. That role must exist before the IAM trust-policy update, so this resource should wait for the Lambda module to finish creating it.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The provisioner updates each Forge role's trust policy to name the Lambda execution role as a principal. That principal must exist when AWS accepts the trust-policy update, so this resource must wait for the Lambda module to create its execution role; currently it can run concurrently with the module.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
null_resource.update_forge_role_trust updates each forge role's trust policy to grant the lambda execution role (arn:...:role/${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator) sts:AssumeRole, but it has no dependency on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda which creates that role. The trust update can run before the trusted lambda role exists, so the relationship should be ordered after the module.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
null_resource.update_forge_role_trust rewrites the forge roles' assume-role trust policies to allow the trust-validator Lambda's execution role to assume them, but it has no dependency on module.forge_trust_validator_lambda, which is the resource that actually creates that IAM role (the trust ARN is hand-built from account_id + prefix). It should be ordered after the module — ideally by referencing the module's real `lambda_role_arn` output instead of reconstructing the ARN.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
null_resource.update_forge_role_trust updates each Forge role's assume-role policy to trust the trust-validator Lambda role (`arn:aws:iam::...:role/${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator`), which is created by module.forge_trust_validator_lambda. It has no dependency on the module, so Terraform can grant trust before that role exists. It should depend on the module so the Lambda role is created first.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
null_resource.update_forge_role_trust embeds the ARN of the IAM role created by module.forge_trust_validator_lambda ("arn:aws:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:role/${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator") into the forge roles' assume-role policy via a local-exec provisioner. Since the ARN is interpolated from var.prefix rather than referencing the module, Terraform orders them independently; if the provisioner runs before the validator role exists, `aws iam update-assume-role-policy` fails with an invalid-principal error. Add a dependency so the lambda module (and its IAM role) is created first.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
null_resource.update_forge_role_trust updates the forge roles' assume-role policy to trust the Lambda execution role "${var.prefix}-forge-trust-validator", which is created inside module.forge_trust_validator_lambda. Because the principal is built from var.prefix as a plain string (not a module attribute reference), Terraform cannot infer that the Lambda (and its IAM role) must exist before the trust policy is updated. On a fresh apply, the null_resource could run before the module and write a trust policy referencing a nonexistent role.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The EventBridge target can become active before the Lambda permission is installed, allowing scheduled invocations to fail authorization. Make the target wait for the permission resource.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
EventBridge needs the Lambda resource-based permission to invoke this function. The target should be created after the permission is installed; currently it only depends on the function module and rule, not on the permission.
